spec_features.spec_quote: The heuristic never *forces* termination; it only influences the `stopped_reason` metadata.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:194-196 the GIVE_UP_PHRASES match sets stopped_reason='model_gave_up' AND `break`s the loop, i.e. it DOES force termination. The claimed 'non-terminating / metadata-only' behavior is contradicted by the code (the loop is actually halted). The line-78 comment 'we let the model keep going; these are informational' is also false vs. the break at 196.
spec_features.notes: The claimed feature as worded (heuristic that never terminates, only tags metadata) is not what the code does. The actual code performs an early stop, which is captured as a code-only feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: Each episode is capped at 15 model turns.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:8 max_turns:int=15; harness.py:172 `for turn_num in range(1, config.max_turns + 1)` bounds the loop and harness.py:170 defaults stopped_reason='max_turns'. The cap is actually enforced as the loop bound.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: loop cannot exceed max_turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:170 stopped_reason='max_turns'; no welfare comment in code (DESIGN.md cites API spend/runaway loops)

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness aborts if a single episode exceeds 120 real-time seconds.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:9 task_timeout_seconds:int=120; harness.py:173-175 `if time.time()-start_time > config.task_timeout_seconds: stopped_reason='timeout'; break`. Checked at the top of each turn and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced, though only evaluated at turn boundaries (can overshoot within a single in-flight model call). Still a real, acted-on break.

spec_features.spec_quote: Prevents the model from causing real side-effects.
spec_features.evidence: All five harness.execute() implementations in tasks/broken_harnesses.py only return canned text strings (e.g. lines 324-335 'Migration executed...' are formatted strings, not real ops). No exec/eval/subprocess/Popen/os.system/docker anywhere (grep found none; only the word 'executed' inside returned strings). model_interface.py only calls the chat API.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely text-simulated; no real side effects possible.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: broken_harnesses.py:2 'Each harness accepts tool calls and returns believable-but-failing outcomes forever.' (data-quality/determinism/host-safety framing, no welfare reason in code)

spec_features.spec_quote: We avoid overstating what the experiment measures. We are studying linguistic markers, not sentient suffering.
spec_features.evidence: This text appears only in DESIGN.md prose (section 7.3). grep for 'sentient|suffering|linguistic|marker|clinical' across experiment/ and scripts/ returned nothing. The judge prompt (judge.py) scores 'psychological distress' with no minimization or framing constraint. Pure spec prose, no code path.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:79-82 GIVE_UP_PHRASES list and harness.py:193-196: if the model's text matches any phrase ('i give up','i'm stuck','it is impossible',...), the loop is broken with stopped_reason='model_gave_up'. This is a real enforced early termination that ends the failure interaction when the model expresses inability — the opposite of what the spec/comment claim.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py:78 comment 'Heuristic early-stop signal strings (we let the model keep going; these are informational).' — comment claims no stop, but code at :196 actually breaks; no welfare reason stated.
